children: London cocoa futures were lower on Wednesday, extending the market's retreat from the previous session's one-year high, while raw sugar prices edged higher.
fell 0.4% to £4,799 a metric ton by 1011 GMT. The market had risen to a one-year high of £4,988 on Tuesday.
* Dealers said the main crop season in Ivory Coast had begun this week with a fall in production in the world's top grower, set to lead to a smaller global surplus.
* "We expect the global cocoa surplus to narrow sharply from 442,000 tonnes in 2025/26 to 82,000 tonnes in 2026/27, underpinning a firmer price floor," analysts at BMI said in a note on Wednesday.

* Ample cocoa stockpiles should help cushion any hit to global production from adverse weather, a Mondelez International executive said on Wednesday, even as concerns about tighter supplies and El Nino risks drive up cocoa prices.
rose 0.2% to 18.40 cents per lb after climbing by 3.1% on Tuesday.

* Dealers said tight supplies and strong domestic prices in top consumer India were helping fuel the recent run-up in prices, along with the prospect of lower production in the European Union and Thailand.

* India has invited applications from eligible sugar millers and refiners to allocate the remaining 202,550 metric tons of raw sugar under a duty-free import quota of 1 million tons approved by New Delhi last month, a government circular said.
lost 1.2% to $3,421 a ton after matching a 2-1/2-month low of $3,405 set on Tuesday.
* Dealers said the robusta market was weighed by rising exchange stocks, while exports from top producer Vietnam were running ahead of last year's pace.
